title: Corroboration of Witness Accounts by Independent Records
keywords: corroboration witness account independent records surveillance device logs location
text:
A witness account gains evidentiary weight when it is corroborated by independent records, such as surveillance footage or device logs, that were created without reference to the account.

Where an independent record places the same person at a different location during an overlapping time interval, the inconsistency must be examined by the reviewing authority before reliance is placed on either source.

Corroboration is a matter of degree. The reviewing authority should consider the directness, independence and provenance of each source rather than counting sources alone.

title: Reliability and Context of Digital Location Records
keywords: phone metadata handset device location cell tower digital record ownership
text:
A digital location record identifies where a device was registered, not necessarily where a particular person was. Ownership and possession of the device during the relevant interval should be established separately.

Location data derived from network towers carries an accuracy radius. The reviewing authority should record that radius and avoid treating the entry as a precise position.

Timestamps on digital records should be checked for clock offsets and time-zone conversion before they are compared with timestamps from other sources.

title: Identification from Surveillance Footage
keywords: cctv surveillance footage identification matching description person camera timestamp
text:
A statement that a person matching a description is visible in footage identifies resemblance, not identity. The basis of the match and the quality of the images should be recorded.

Camera clocks may differ from real time. The offset should be documented before the footage timestamp is compared with other time evidence.

Where footage and a witness account are consistent, the footage should be checked for continuity between the frames relied upon.

title: Approximation and Recollection of Time in Testimony
keywords: testimony recollection approximate time cannot remember uncertainty hearing witness
text:
A witness who gives an approximate time, or who says the exact time cannot be recalled, is expressing the limits of recollection. That expression alone is not an indicator of the reliability of the account.

Approximate times should be compared with other sources using a reasonable tolerance rather than as exact instants.

title: Electronic Records and Chain of Custody
keywords: electronic record chain of custody provenance hash extraction handling digital evidence
text:
An electronic record should be accompanied by documentation of who extracted it, when, and by what method, so that its provenance can be reviewed.

Where custody documentation is missing or incomplete, the gap should be noted for the reviewing authority.

title: Reconciling Differences Between Statements
keywords: statement inconsistency prior statement testimony contradiction explain variation
text:
Differences between an earlier statement and later testimony should be identified with reference to the exact passages compared.

Minor variations in detail are to be distinguished from differences on a material point. The witness should have had an opportunity to explain the difference.

title: Notice Periods in Commercial Contract Termination
keywords: contract termination notice period written notice breach commercial agreement clause waiver
text:
Where a contract prescribes a notice period for termination, the party terminating must show that written notice was given in the manner and within the time the contract requires.

Conduct suggesting waiver of a notice requirement should be examined against the wording of the clause and the surrounding correspondence.

title: Documentary Proof of Possession and Title
keywords: property possession title deed register sale document ownership boundary lease
text:
Title documents and registers are the primary source for ownership. Evidence of possession is relevant but is assessed separately from title.

Where two documents describe the same parcel differently, the descriptions should be compared clause by clause before either is preferred.
